- **How the guard reads these commands now:**
  - **Short options:** `cp` letters `abdfHilLnPprRsTuvxZ` take no value and `S t` take one. `mv`: `bfinTuvZ` / `S t`. `install`: `bcCdDpsTvZ` / `g m o S t`. A value can be joined (`-S.t`, `-oroot`, `-m+t`) or the next word (`-S -t`).
  - **`-Z`** takes no value, so `cp -Zt <folder> X` is still judged as a copy into that folder.
  - **Long options:** every unique prefix is accepted, the way `getopt_long` does it (`--pa` means parents). Options that need a value take it after `=` or as the next word; optional values only after `=`.
  - **`--`:** nothing after it is read as an option. A lone `-` is an operand.
  - **Refused as doubt:** `cp --parents` in any spelling and the `--path` alias; unknown options; ambiguous prefixes (`--p`); a value given to an option that takes none; a value missing at the end of the command.
  - **Backups:** with `-b`, `--backup`, `-S` or `--suffix`, the file `<file><suffix>` is judged next to each replaced file that isn't a folder, and also for the destination folder of `mv -T`. An empty suffix, or one containing `/`, is read as `~`, which is what the tools do.
  - **Checked against the real tools:** the option tables match `cp`/`mv`/`install` on this machine. I checked with a script in my temp folder (every long name is known, its value type matches, and nothing in `--help` is missing). This is not a committed test.

discoveries:
- `cp --path` is an old alias for `--parents` that coreutils 9.4 still accepts. It is now refused too.
- `mv -b -T <dir> <own folder>` would have put the backup `W2-90~` directly in the root, which the KPIs forbid. A suffix that turns an own-folder file name into the marker's name would have replaced the marker. Both are now refused, and builder tests cover them.
- `src/gov/guard/protected.py` (outside my allowed paths) imports `_cp_operands`. I left that function unchanged for it, so its second-name reading still uses the old option reader.

risks:
- If `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set, the tools read every word after the first operand as an operand. A word starting with `-` there (for example `-t`) is not judged as a file landing in the destination. The destination folder itself is still judged. Not tested.
- Numbered backups (`.~N~`) and `SIMPLE_BACKUP_SUFFIX` are judged only by the `~` name, or the given suffix, in the same folder.
- The tables are for coreutils 9.4. Under a newer version an unknown option is refused (fails closed), but a letter that starts taking a value would be misread.
